instructions: Create an Excel report from Jira for epics whose summary or Epic Name contains the feature keyword, excluding any epic whose summary or Epic Name contains any of the exclude keywords.
If multiple include keywords match the same epic, assign that epic to the most specific matching include keyword only. A more specific or exact keyword wins over a broader keyword.
Direct epic keys such as PROJ-1234 can be used as include keywords. They should load that exact epic only, and if the same epic is also matched by a broader keyword it must still load only once.
When an epic is included by exact epic key, use the epic's human-readable Epic Name as the Feature label if available, otherwise fall back to Epic Summary.

A special include keyword in the form all ProjectName should load all epics in that Jira project. ProjectName may be the Jira project name or the Jira project key such as PROJ. If a more specific include keyword also matches an epic from that project, the more specific include keyword should own that epic.
Create one workbook per report year. Name files roadmap YYYY.xlsx, for example roadmap 2026.xlsx and roadmap 2027.xlsx.
Only refresh rows that are new, blank, in progress, or on hold.
Do not recalculate or overwrite any field for rows already marked done or rejected.
Sort rows by Start date ascending, then End date ascending, then Substream name ascending.
Rows without a Start date should be ordered by End date, and rows without both dates should be ordered by Substream name.

weekly_sheet.name: weekly
rules: Weekly tab should contain only a feature selector and the weekly progress table.
Use Feature name as the selector label next to the dropdown.
Weekly progress must be driven by the selected feature only.
Dates should show the week start and week end as MMM-DD – MMM-DD.
Weeks should show the ISO week number.
Task counts should split into Tasks group and Bugs group by Task type from the tasks sheet.
Tasks+Bugs total = sum of Tasks done/rejected plus Bugs done/rejected.
Required appears only on the latest week row and uses the same number as summary Required for ETA.
Net task flow group = Created, Net, Scope; Scope should use 🚀 Growing for non-negative net and 🔥 Burining for negative net.
The feature selector should reuse the same feature names as summary and tasks.
Use the workbook's existing emoji style for Scope.

Row layout: row 1 = Feature name label, row 2 = feature dropdown (A2) and Required label/value (F2/G2), row 3 = a blank spacer row, row 4 = group sub-headers for both the weekly table and the epic side table, row 5 = column headers for both tables, row 6+ = data. Freeze rows 1 through 5.

Epic name (epic side table) shows the epic's real Jira summary text (Epic Summary), not the derived/trimmed Substream label. Fall back to Substream, then to the Feature label, only when no Epic Summary was captured for that epic (e.g. older data from before this field existed). This is a display-only value — the feature dropdown filter keys on a separate LookupKey (Feature|seq), not on this text, so changing it cannot affect the filter.

formatting: Use Arial 10 everywhere, bold headers, clickable Jira-key hyperlinks in Link, Feature = the exact keyword that matched that epic, Substream = use Epic Summary when Epic Summary and Epic Name differ, otherwise use Epic Name; then trim the exact matched feature keyword from the beginning only, red task text with white font when Delta ETA > 1, yellow italic Task/Status/Start for in progress, gray for rejected, freeze top row, auto-size columns to content.
Tasks sheet column widths: Feature = 137, Substream = 137, Task = 517, Epic = hug content, week columns P+ = 42.
Starting after Created week in the tasks sheet, add Epic as a helper column, then add week columns 1 through 52 in the header row.
Use a green fill color of #2EC67E for task-week cells when a task was in work during that ISO week.
Store each row's Epic key in a visible helper column in the tasks sheet so summary rebuilds can preserve the Epics list without another Jira pull.
For each task row, fill a week cell green if that row had any work time in that ISO week.
Done rows should always color their completion week, even if the start or end date falls on a non-business day.
Done rows stop coloring after their completion week and do not color future weeks.
In progress rows can color multiple weeks from Start through the report date.
On hold rows should color only the weeks where work happened before the hold pause, and should not color pause-only weeks.
Format all workbook dates as MMM-DD, for example Jan-01.
Link should display only the Jira key but stay clickable.
Numeric cells should not show a trailing dot for integers. Display 2 instead of 2., while still displaying decimals like 2.5 when present.
Delta ETA should be blank for on hold and non-done rows.
Positive Delta ETA should render with a leading + but remain numeric.
Task should turn red with white text only when Delta ETA > 1.
Story should map to Task, and any other issue types should stay as-is.
Rejected rows should stay gray.
Each unique Feature value should have its own distinct, nice-looking fill color in the Feature cell, and the text color must remain readable against that background.
Feature colors should use at least 50 distinct colors before reusing any color, and the colors should still look good together when multiple features appear in the same report.
If the matched keyword is the full Epic Name and Epic Summary is the same as Epic Name, trimming it from Substream should leave Substream blank.
Trim only when the matched keyword appears at the beginning of Epic Name.
When trimming from the beginning, also trim any separator directly after the keyword, such as ':', '-', or spaces.
Do not trim keyword text from the middle of Epic Name.
If Epic Summary and Epic Name are different, prefer Epic Summary for Substream instead of leaving Substream blank.
feature_status: Add a Feature status column after Link.
Check tasks by Feature name in the tasks tab.
Feature status must be recalculated on every report run from the task rows for each Feature, so reruns always apply the general rule again.
If a Feature has at least one in-progress row, set Feature status = blank for every task row of that Feature.
If a Feature has 0 in-progress rows and at least one blank row, set Feature status = on hold for every task row of that Feature.
If all task rows for a Feature are blank, set Feature status = open for every task row of that Feature.
If a Feature has 0 blank rows and 0 in-progress rows, set Feature status = done for every task row of that Feature.
Use the Feature status column for visibility control: blank rows are visible by default, and open, on hold, and done rows are hidden by the Excel filter.
If a report rerun changes the current task mix for a Feature, recompute Feature status for every task row of that Feature according to the same general rule.
feature_settings: When a new feature keyword is added during setup, ask for Expected pace, tasks /w for that feature.
Store Expected pace, tasks /w per feature keyword in settings and reuse it on later runs unless the user changes it.

On update, if the include/exclude keywords stay the same, refresh only rows whose current task state is new, blank, in progress, or on hold; keep done and rejected rows from the existing workbook unchanged.
On update, if new include keywords are added, keep the existing workbook rows and also pull tasks for the newly added keywords so the report grows without losing already completed or rejected rows.

If saved settings exist and the current report file exists, the launcher should first offer a short action choice: update/upd to update the existing report, new to build a fresh new report with the same settings, or edit to edit the settings.
task_type: If the issue type is Story, treat it as Task.
Keep other issue types as is.
status_mapping: In Progress or In QA... -> in progress
Code Review and Progress Done are also part of the active in progress segment for lifecycle reconstruction, even though they do not need separate report rows.
Done, QA Prod Done, In Validation -> done
everything else in backlog/todo/definition style -> blank
QA On hold or Track/Blocked/On hold -> create a separate on hold row
If a task returns from on hold to backlog/todo/definition, emit a trailing blank/open row for the new current state so the later reopen wins over the older hold segment.
dates: Normal row: Start = first In Progress; if none, first In QA...; if the task is already done and never entered either state, use End as Start.
Normal row: End = first QA Prod Done; if missing, first Done.

If a task never entered In Progress or In QA..., and it reaches done through terminal statuses only, collapse the done row to use the earliest terminal End date as both Start and End rather than creating Start > End.
Hold/resume cycle: keep the hold row and create a new resumed row when the task re-enters In Progress.
Hold row: Start = first In Progress before the hold, End = date the task entered on hold.
Resumed row: Start = first In Progress after the hold, not the original first In Progress.
Resumed row: End = QA Prod Done; if missing, use Done.

If a task goes on hold and then reaches done or rejected without a resumed In Progress segment, absorb that hold into the terminal row so the final row spans from the original active start through the terminal end.
On hold is only a specific status transition to QA On hold or Track/Blocked/On hold.
The purpose of the separate on hold row is to pause elapsed work tracking. Time spent while the task is on hold must not count toward Days in Work or Delta ETA.

A resumed row represents a new active work segment after the hold. Days in Work must be counted separately for each active segment and then reflected through the generated rows so hold time is excluded from ETA overrun calculations.
If a task moves directly from on hold to done or rejected, the terminal row Start must use the most recent active segment start before that hold, not the first historical start of the issue.

If a task later re-enters active work, on hold, or blank/open after an earlier done or rejected transition, treat that earlier done or rejected transition as provisional and do not keep it as a final row. A task with current blank status is not done — any prior done that preceded the blank transition must be discarded.

Merge multiple hold periods into a single on hold row whenever possible. Days in Work math is identical regardless of how many hold rows exist, so fewer rows is always better. Merge a new hold into the existing hold row when either: (a) the resumed in-progress started on the same day or the next calendar day after the previous hold ended, or (b) the resumed segment had no real active work (no new business days) before going on hold again. Only create a separate hold row when neither condition is met.

If a task enters on hold and then resumes in progress, reaches done, or reaches rejected later that same day, skip the on hold row entirely — the hold was a transient status change with no meaningful pause.
When a task is on hold, week coloring must stop at the first hold week and must not continue through pause-only weeks.
When a task returns from on hold to in progress, week coloring must resume only from the resumed active segment forward.
fallback_rules: Use changelog dates only for open or active rows (in progress, on hold) that still need date updates.
For newly added done tasks, do not guess Start from created or updated.
If a realistic Start cannot be determined cheaply, leave it blank.
Always use Jira resolution date as End for newly added done tasks.
If ETA is missing, leave Delta ETA blank.
Exclude only tasks whose Start date exists and is in a previous report year. Tasks with no Start date should remain in the tasks tab.

The current report year is the year of the report run date. If the report is run in July 2026, tasks with Start dates in 2025 or earlier are excluded, tasks with Start dates in 2026 are included, and tasks with no Start date are also included. If the report is run in January 2027, create a new workbook for 2027 and exclude only tasks whose Start date is in 2026 or earlier.
metrics: ETA = the Jira field that represents ETA in the current Jira project; if no such field exists, leave ETA blank.
Days in Work = business days between Start and End, inclusive; if End is blank, count through the report run date.
Delta ETA = Days in Work - ETA.
Only populate Delta ETA for done rows.
For issues with hold/resume cycles, hold time must not count as work time.
For a resumed done row, Days in Work and Delta ETA must use cumulative active business days across all active segments of that issue, excluding hold time.

columns: Feature = the feature label used to group related epics and tasks.
Substream = the secondary feature label; use Epic Summary when Epic Summary and Epic Name differ, otherwise use Epic Name, then trim the matched feature keyword from the beginning only.
Task type = normalized task type, with Story mapped to Task.
Status = lifecycle status used by the report, such as blank, in progress, on hold, done, or rejected.
Start = the first active work date for the row.
End = the completion date for the row.
Done week = ISO week number of End.
ETA = the Jira ETA field, if available.
Days in Work = business days between Start and End, or through the report date if End is blank.
Delta ETA = Days in Work minus ETA, only for done rows when ETA exists.
Created date = Jira created date for the task.
Created week = ISO week number of Created date.
Epic = visible helper column containing the Jira Epic key for the row; it should hug content and remain clickable.
Feature status = helper flag with values blank, open, on hold, or done; the value is recomputed from the current task rows on every report run.
Weeks 1-52 = one column per ISO week of the report year; a green cell means the task had active work in that week.
rules: Week columns start immediately after the Epic helper column and continue through 52 columns.
The header row for week columns must show week numbers 1 through 52.
Highlight the current report week header cell in yellow.
Use green #2EC67E for week cells that were worked during that week.
Tasks that are done must stop filling future week cells after the completion week.
Tasks that are on hold must stop filling week cells after the hold begins.
If a task returns from on hold to in progress, week-cell filling resumes only from the resumed active segment forward.
A week cell is green only when that task had active work during that ISO week, not merely because the task exists in the report.
Done and on-hold status transitions are stop points for future green filling.
Keep the week coloring aligned to active work segments, excluding pause-only time from the task-week grid.

summary_sheet.name: summary
summary_sheet.report_date: Show Updated at in A1 and the report date in A2, above the summary table. Use the current report run date each time the report is generated or auto-updated.
rules: This section defines the summary tab.

Use visual divider lines to group the summary metrics into these blocks: Feature; Pace - tasks per week (done+rejected) / Expected / ETA / Actual / ETA from actual / Required for ETA; Status / Scope done / Delivered / Δ ETA, mo; TTM, mo / Estimated / Actual / Hold, mo / Δ, %; Totals tasks / Created / Done / Rejected / Remaining; Tasks Δ ETA / Δ ETA > 1d / Δ ETA, %; Epics.
Place divider lines immediately after Feature, after Required for ETA, after Δ ETA, mo, after Δ, %, after Tasks remaining, and before Epics.
Build the summary sheet from the tasks tab data. Do not pull these counts separately from Jira a second time.
Show Updated at label in A1 and the date in A2 instead of Report date.
All workbook date cells must use the DD.MMM.YY format (e.g. 04.Aug.27).

Summary sheet styling: wrap text in summary cells, align content to the top vertically in all summary cells, align the Updated at label/date area to the left, render Scope done as the only progress percentage + bar cell with wrapped text, make all summary rows hug their content height, and freeze rows 1 through 4 AND column A (Feature), so Feature stays visible on horizontal scroll.
Summary column widths: Feature = 34, Epics = 179, Scope done = 28, all other summary columns = 94.
Row layout: row 1 = Updated at label, row 2 = the date alone, row 3 = group sub-header labels (A3 is blank — Feature has no group label), row 4 = column headers, row 5+ = data.
Row 3 summary group labels should align to the bottom across columns B through Q.

Sort the summary tab by the first available summary date in this priority: Delivery date ascending, then the earliest of (ETA, ETA based on actual pace) ascending. Any row with no summary date should sort after all rows with a summary date, and blank-date rows should then sort alphabetically by Feature.
Epics = comma-separated Epic keys assigned to that feature, for example PROJ-1232, PROJ-2131.
The Epics cell should be clickable and open a Jira search containing the listed epic keys.
Keep rejected rows in the tasks tab, but exclude rejected tasks from all summary calculations.
Task created = total number of created tasks for the feature.
Tasks created = all unique Jira tasks in all epics assigned to a single feature, including rejected tasks.
Tasks done = unique non-rejected tasks assigned to the feature whose final/current task state is done.
Tasks rejected = unique tasks assigned to the feature whose final/current task state is rejected.
Tasks remaining = unique non-rejected tasks assigned to the feature whose final/current task state is blank, in progress, or on hold.
Progress = (tasks done + tasks rejected) / all created tasks; it should reach 100% when all tasks for the feature are resolved.

Scope done = a visual cell after Required for ETA and before Delivered that renders the same scope-completion percentage as wrapped percentage text plus a horizontal bar. Use the formula TEXT(MIN(1,MAX(0,scope_done)),"0%")&CHAR(10)&REPT(...) so the percentage is on its own line above the bar. Use text color #64487D.
Scope done column should use width 28.
Epic helper column in the tasks sheet should hug content width and the Epic value should be clickable.
The tasks sheet should default-filter Feature status to show only blank rows and hide done, on hold, and open rows automatically on each refresh.

Actual, tasks /w = the feature-wide average completed-task pace, calculated as tasks done divided by the number of feature-active weeks (weeks that contain at least one done or in-progress task row). Show it for all features that have at least one done task.

ETA from actual = the projected delivery date implied by the current feature-wide actual pace. Recompute it on every report update, because it changes when pace changes. Show it for all features that have at least one done task.
Net task flow (last 4w avg) = (tasks done + tasks rejected) - tasks created, averaged over the last 4 done weeks in the tasks tab. A negative value means we create more tasks than we close.
Display 4-week average task counts as whole numbers.

Expected = the planned delivery rate entered during setup, or computed backwards from ETA when ETA is provided. In that case, use first done task as the anchor and calculate how many tasks per week are needed to complete all created tasks from the first done task through ETA.
ETA = first done task date + expected pace. If ETA is provided during setup, use the provided ETA instead.

Use completed-task history only for the ETA anchor date. Ignore blank, in progress, on hold, and rejected rows when choosing that anchor. Prefer the first End date of a done task; if it is unavailable, fall back to the first Start date of a done task.
Delivery date = the End date of the latest done task in the feature, but only for completed features.
Estimated TTM, mo = ETA minus the first done-task date, expressed in calendar months.

IMPORTANT — row semantics for on hold: a task-lifecycle row's Start/End is always the active work burst that happened BEFORE that row's terminal status, even when that status is 'on hold'. E.g. a row 'on hold | 20.Nov | 24.Nov' means the task was actively worked 20-24 Nov and only became on hold at the end of that range — it does NOT mean the task sat paused for those days. The actual pause is the gap between one row's End and the next row's Start for that same task, not the on-hold row's own date range. Do not filter active-work-day calculations by status label (e.g. do not exclude rows just because Status = 'on hold' or 'rejected') — any row with both a Start and an End date represents real work; only the blank/backlog row has no dates.

Actual TTM, mo = distinct business days where ANY task in the feature had a work burst, unioned across every lifecycle row of every task (not summed — summing double-counts days where multiple tasks were worked in parallel). Divide the day count by business days per month (30.4375 * 5/7 ≈ 21.74) to get months.

Hold, mo = business days inside the feature's own working span (from its first active business day to its last) where the active-work union above has no coverage — i.e. real idle/paused time within the feature's lifetime, not before or after it. This is what reconciles a feature that looks faster than estimated (low Actual TTM) with a later-than-ETA delivery (positive Δ ETA, mo): the gap is time spent paused, not time spent working.
Δ ETA, mo = Delivered minus ETA, expressed in calendar months. Positive means the ETA was missed; negative means delivery was early. Color it the same as Δ, % (red for positive, green for negative).
Δ, % = (Actual TTM, mo - Estimated TTM, mo) / Estimated TTM, mo. Populate it only when both TTM values exist and Estimated TTM, mo is greater than zero.
Required pace from TODAY to meet ETA = tasks remaining / remaining weeks until ETA. Leave blank if ETA is in the past.
Feature start date = earliest task Start date for the feature; if none exists, use earliest Created date.
Task created = total number of created tasks for the feature.
Δ ETA > 1d = done tasks only where Delta ETA > 1.
Δ ETA, % = (Δ ETA > 1d) / tasks done.
Remove the Last 4w avg group from the summary sheet entirely.
Round calculated numeric values in the summary sheet to full numbers.
If Δ ETA, % is positive, render the Δ, % cell value red and keep the row fill unchanged, except the Feature cell keeps its feature color.
If Δ ETA, % is negative, render the Δ, % cell value green and keep the row fill unchanged, except the Feature cell keeps its feature color.
If a feature is done, fill the whole summary row light gray, except the Feature cell keeps its feature color.

If a feature currently has at least one task in progress and there is no ETA delta coloring, fill the whole summary row light yellow and italicize the row, except the Feature cell keeps its feature color. Do not change the text color or link styling for that row.

link: Use https://{JIRA_HOST}/browse/ISSUEKEY (the configured Jira host) as the hyperlink target and display only ISSUEKEY as anchor text.
